cities.d: the capital's old town is characterized by old stone streets and houses. Escaldes-Engordany, next door, hosts a hot spa, a perfume museum and an art gallery

x.around: You should be able to walk around most of Andorra la Vella. The town is really in two parts. There is the newer section at the north end of the town that is very commercial with lots of shops. The other half is the older half, down across the river and to the south and west. This also has shops, places to eat and the historic part.

hidden.d: Romanesque church dating from the 12th century. It is obligatory to reserve by phone.

This visitor centre has useful information on the leisure activities offered in the Madriu-Perafita-Claror valley, as well as facts on the tasks carried out to manage the valley and promote the values that have made it a UNESCO…
Park with small pond and public toilets.
Art gallery for temporary exhibitions. It is worth going in just for the great view over the river (including a glass floor) and up the valley.
A sculpture by Salvador Dalí featuring his melting clock.
A spa, sauna and swimming complex. It is at the top of the town in the dramatic glass spire structure.
A hot spring water fountain, considered one of the hottest in Europe (70ºC). Bring a water bottle, but be careful.
Modernist style, designed by the architect Josep Puig i Cadafalch. It is not possible to visit inside because it is a private home. From the 1930s.

x.intro: Andorra la Vella is the capital of Andorra. It is a small alpine city that draws visitors primarily for skiing, hiking and tax-free shopping. Even if those activities don't appeal to you, there is enough in the city to fill a day or two. There is a large spa complex, an interesting old town, and several museums This article also covers the adjoining parish of Escaldes-Engordany.

must.d: This church in the old part of the city dates from the 12th century, but was restored in 1940 by the Moderniste architect Josep Puig y Cadafalch who also undertook important works in Barcelona.
This bridge dates from medieval times but is still in perfect condition. Nearby there is a metallic sculpture made by the Valencian sculptor Andreu Alfaro.

Romanesque style, dated from 12th century and restored on 20th century. It is notable the disproportion between the nave and the 17-m bell tower. It is obligatory to reserve beforehand. Free-guided tours.

n.es: iglesia de San Miguel de Engolasters

cities.d: south of Santa Coloma towards the border with Spain

hidden.d: It is at 1,650 m. Dated from 13th century – Romanesque style. Every year, on the last Saturday in May happens a pilgrimage with the attendance of most of the people of Sant Julià de Lòria and many from elsewhere in the country.
Church dated from 11th century – Romanesque style. It is outside of Nagol village. It is obligatory to reserve beforehand. Free-guided tours.
A museum of tobacco, smoking and smuggling housed in a former tobacco factory.

x.intro: Sant Julia de Loria (correctly Sant Julià de Lòria) lies on the border to Spain in the southern parish (administrative division) in Andorra between Andorra La Vella and Spain.

cities.d: has the ruins of a Romanesque church and several small museums

x.around: Within the town of Encamp, you can get by with walking. There is also Funibus, which is a bus service run by the parish. Funibus takes passengers around Encamp and connect to the Funicamp gondola. The service is free and not restricted to skiers.

hidden.d: Displays automobiles from various eras from 1880s to 1970s. It also has over 100 bicycles from historical to present day.
Located within the same building as the national hydroelectric company, this museum shows how electricity transformed Andorra since its arrival in 1934.
A house converted into a museum. This house was inhabited until 1947 and shows the lifestyle of Andorran people from late 19th century to early 20th century.
A small museum with jewellery, textiles and paper collections dedicated to religious text. It is located next to Santa Eulalia church.

n.en: Museu d'Art Sacre de Santa Eulàlia

x.intro: Encamp is a parish (administrative division) and town, 4 km north-east of Andorra La Vella and close to the French border at Pas de la Casa (2085 m).

cities.d: small town and parish about 5 miles north of Andorra La Vella. You can access Arinsal—Pal ski area from it directly

x.around: The parish runs its own bus routes, numbered M1 to M4. A single La Massana local bus trip costs . * M1 La Massana - Erts - Arinsal - La Massana * M2 La Massana - Erts - Pal - La Massana * M3 La Massana - Escas - Sispony - Anoys - L'Aldosa - La Massana * M4 La Massana - L'Adosa - Anoys - Sispony - Escas - La Massana
x.intro: La Massana lies in the western border parish (administrative division) of the same name and en route to the town of Ordino in Andorra between Andorra La Vella and France.

must.d: Romanesque church from the 12th century. It is in the village of Pal. An interesting feature to note is the Romanesque Lombard belfry, one of the most interesting in Andorra. It is obligatory to reserve beforehand.
Built in the Romanesque style. It is in the old part of La Massana. It is obligatory to reserve beforehand.

n.en: Church of Sant Iscle and Santa Victòria
n.es: iglesia de San Acisclo y Santa Victoria

next.d: village: This village preserves the typical appearance of the traditional Pyrenean village and enters a Pal for Special Protection, passed in 1997.

cities.d: over 10 km of cross-country ski trails, and some museums and churches to visit

hidden.d: A museum with a collection of miniature items collected by Nicolai Siadristy. A large number of Matryoshka dolls, miniature art, decorated Easter egg and more.

x.intro: Ordino is the northernmost parish (administrative division) and town of Andorra between Andorra La Vella and France. It has the fewest inhabitants of all Andorran parishes but covers almost the largest area.

must.d: A noble house converted into a museum showing the daily life of Andorrans. It is co-located with Museum Postal.
Museum documenting the postal service of Andorra. It is co-located with Museum Casa d'Areny-Plandolit.

next.d: ski resort that lies in the northwestern corner of the border parish (administrative division) of Ordino.

cities.d: has an Olympic size ice skating rink and entertainment complex

hidden.d: Jul-Aug every day, 10AM-1PM; 3PM-6PM. Free-guided tours. The rest of the year only at mass hours. This is an 11th – 12th century church, one of the most beautiful build from Andorra.

x.intro: Canillo is a parish (administrative division) and town 12km NE of the capital of Andorra between Andorra La Vella and the French border at Pas de la Casa (2085m).

cities.d: small village and ski resort in the north west

x.around: There is a bus service between Arinsal and Andorra La Vella, passing through La Massana. It is not very regular so it is worth checking the timetable before planning any trips. The cost is reasonable.
x.intro: Arinsal is a village in Andorra, a small mountainous country in the Pyrenees mountains at the head of a valley. The old village part is clearly evident, but because it is also a ski resort it has grown a lot and has quite a number of hotels catering to this trade. As a result though outside the ski season the place is pretty much closed up including some of the bars and restaurants.

cities.d: a town that preserves the typical appearance of the traditional Pyrenean village

x.around: Pal is connected to the winter sports resort of Pal-Arinsal (Vallnord area) by the CS-420 road. The station is 2 km south of the village.
x.intro: Pal in Andorra lies in the northwestern border parish (administrative division) of La Massana and is a skiing village in the same area as Arinsal. It is connected to Arinsal by cable car.

intro: Andorra is a small, mountainous country in Western Europe, up in the Pyrenees between France and Spain. Full of beautiful mountains and charming old villages, the country thrives on tourism, mainly visitors from nearby countries who come for shopping, skiing, hiking, and banking.
